name: @kb/mobile
description: Expo SDK 57 client for KnowledgeBot AI. Deliberately NOT "type": "module" — babel.config.js, metro.config.js and jest.config.js are loaded as CommonJS by Metro and Jest, and flipping this field breaks all three at once with three unrelated-looking errors. Versions are split into two groups on purpose: EXACT pins for the stack the ADRs and skills fix, and SDK-aligned RANGES for the packages whose patch level must come from `npx expo install --check` rather than from anyone's memory (see the comment blocks below).

//versions.exact-pins: expo, expo-router, expo-secure-store, react-native, react, @tanstack/react-query and @kb/contracts are fixed by expo-react-native / ADR-020 / ADR-028. .npmrc sets save-exact=true so nothing here may grow a caret by accident.
//versions.react-19.2.3: NOT 19.2.0, and the difference is a hard resolver failure rather than a preference. react-native@0.86.2 declares `peerDependencies: {react: "^19.2.3"}`, and .npmrc sets auto-install-peers=false — so an unsatisfied peer stays unsatisfied and is reported, not quietly conjured. 19.2.3 is also what Expo's own version map returns for SDK 57 (`facebookReactVersion`/`relatedPackages.react` at api.expo.dev/v2/versions/latest), which is the number `expo install --check` compares against. react-dom moves in LOCKSTEP with react: the two ship from one React release and a split between them produces renderer/reconciler mismatches that surface as unrelated-looking runtime errors, not as an install failure. react-dom is here for jest-expo's jsdom project and react-native-web, not for the app itself.
//versions.sdk-aligned-ranges: Every `~57.0.0` entry is an Expo-versioned package whose patch level is owned by the SDK, not by us. `npx expo install --check` rewrites them to the versions SDK 57 was released against; `npx expo-doctor` fails the build if they drift. react-native-safe-area-context and react-native-screens are expo-router's required peers and are NOT Expo-versioned, so their ranges are the ones expo install resolves first — do not trust the numbers here until that command has run.
//versions.react-native-screens-4.26.0: That warning was load-bearing: the scaffold's `~4.20.0` was a guess and it was wrong. expo-router@57.0.10 declares `react-native-screens: ^4.26.0`, so 4.20.0 was a genuinely unmet peer (pnpm: `unmet peer react-native-screens@^4.26.0: found 4.20.0`), and Expo's SDK 57 map agrees on ~4.26.0. Unmet rather than merely stale matters because .npmrc sets auto-install-peers=false — nothing was going to reconcile this, and the symptom would have been a missing native screen API at runtime rather than a failed install. react-native-safe-area-context@~5.7.0 was checked in the same pass and is correct.
//versions.jest-expo: jest-expo's MAJOR must equal the Expo SDK major. SDK 57 => jest-expo ~57.0.0. A jest-expo from a different major silently ships the wrong Babel transform and the wrong module mocks.
//versions.@jest/globals-29.7.0: DECLARED rather than dropped, and the choice is deliberate. jest.setup.ts and all three suites import `describe/it/expect/jest` from '@jest/globals' by name instead of relying on the ambient globals the runner injects — which is what keeps `tsc --noEmit` honest, because an ambient `jest` global makes a typo'd matcher name compile. The package was only ever present transitively (jest-expo depends on ^29.2.1), and pnpm's strict layout does not put a transitive dependency on the resolution path, so all four files failed with TS2307 while the tests themselves ran fine. Pinned to 29.7.0 to match the runner exactly: @jest/globals ships from the same release as jest, and the 30.x pnpm offers here would pair 30's type definitions with a 29 runtime. Note this must NOT be 'solved' by adding @types/jest — that reintroduces the ambient globals this import style exists to avoid, and the two disagree.
//versions.@react-native/jest-preset-0.86.2: A REQUIRED peer of jest-expo@57.0.3 (`"@react-native/jest-preset": "^0.86.2"`, and NOT listed in its peerDependenciesMeta as optional), and it was missing. With auto-install-peers=false nothing conjured it, so `pnpm test` did not fail a test — it failed to START, on a jest Validation Error from jest-expo/jest-preset.js: 'The React Native Jest preset that jest-expo relies on has moved to a separate package.' The RN preset used to ship inside react-native itself as `react-native/jest-preset`; RN 0.86 moved it out, jest-expo now requires the new package first and only falls back to the old path, and both lookups miss here. Version tracks react-native EXACTLY (0.86.2 = jest-expo's own devDependency pin and the react-native in this manifest); a jest preset from a different RN patch line configures transforms and haste settings for a runtime this app does not run.
//versions.formerly-unresolved: `jest` and `react-test-renderer` were "*" until the first lockfile was generated, on the rule that their correct values are whatever jest-expo@57 resolves against rather than whatever anyone remembers. That resolution has now happened and both stars are gone — a "*" surviving into a committed lockfile is a review finding (ADR-020), and these two were the last unpinned specifiers in the repo. Re-derive, do not re-guess: `npx expo install --check`.
//versions.jest-29.7.0: The Expo SDK 57 test stack is jest 29, NOT 30. Expo's version map lists `jest: ~29.7.0` for SDK 57, jest-expo@57.0.3 depends on @jest/globals, babel-jest, jest-environment-jsdom, jest-snapshot and @jest/create-cache-key-function all at ^29.2.1, and react-native@0.86.2 itself depends on babel-jest@^29.7.0 and jest-environment-node@^29.7.0. The old "*" resolved to jest 30.4.2, which does NOT fail the install: jest-expo declares no `jest` peer and @testing-library/react-native only asks for >=29.0.0, so nothing objected while the tree carried a jest-30 runner driving a jest-29 preset, environment and snapshot format. 29.7.0 is the newest 29.x, so this is the top of the correct major, not a downgrade to an old patch.
//versions.react-test-renderer-19.2.3: Pinned to EXACTLY the version jest-expo@57.0.3 lists as a direct dependency (`"react-test-renderer": "19.2.3"`, exact, not a range). Two reasons it may not float. First, correctness: react-test-renderer declares `peerDependencies: {react: "^19.2.3"}` at 19.2.3 and each later patch raises that floor to its own version — the old "*" resolved to 19.2.8, whose `^19.2.8` peer no react 19.2.x below it can satisfy, so the star was unsatisfiable against ANY react this SDK allows. Second, deduplication: a version here that differs from jest-expo's brings a second react-test-renderer into the tree, and a renderer built against a different React copy is the classic duplicate-React hazard — hooks resolve against the wrong dispatcher and the failure reads as a nonsense 'invalid hook call' in a test that changed nothing. Matching the pin exactly collapses both copies into one.
//versions.@testing-library/react-native: v13.x is a HARD constraint: v12 predates React 19 and its renderer assumptions break under RN 0.86.
//versions.babel-preset-expo-and-babel-runtime: BOTH ARE DIRECT devDependencies BECAUSE OF pnpm's ISOLATED LINKER, and neither is optional. babel.config.js names 'babel-preset-expo' by string, and Babel resolves a preset from the CONFIG FILE's directory — apps/mobile — not from wherever the tool that loaded it lives. Under npm's flat layout the copy that `expo` and `jest-expo` depend on is hoisted to the app's node_modules and the string resolves by accident; under pnpm only DIRECT dependencies are linked there, so it does not. The failure is not a test failure: `pnpm test` cannot START, on `Cannot find module 'babel-preset-expo'` raised from inside @babel/core's plugin resolver, with a stack listing only jest internals and no mention of this app. Metro fails the same way on the first JSX file. @babel/runtime is the second half of the same problem: babel-preset-expo compiles with `@babel/plugin-transform-runtime`, so every transformed module emits `require('@babel/runtime/helpers/…')` resolved from the APP, and with the preset fixed the next error is `Cannot find module '@babel/runtime/helpers/interopRequireDefault' from jest.setup.ts`. Versions are exact and match what the tree already resolved transitively (babel-preset-expo 57.0.6 via expo@57.0.10 and jest-expo@57.0.3; @babel/runtime 7.29.7), so declaring them adds no new resolution — it only makes an existing one reachable. babel-preset-expo's `react-refresh` peer is satisfied from the same graph; do NOT 'fix' any of this with node-linker=hoisted, which would silently re-hoist every other transitive package and hide the next occurrence of exactly this bug.
//versions.no-jest-native: @testing-library/jest-native is DEPRECATED and is deliberately absent. Its matchers merged into RNTL 12.4+, so adding it back double-registers toHaveTextContent/toBeVisible etc. — the second registration wins silently and the failure messages stop matching the assertions.
